title: Pluto's Eternal Orbit
hook: Your great-grandparents saw Pluto's start, but it won't finish?
script: Your great-grandparents saw Pluto's start, but it won't finish? What if a whole planet hadn't finished one 'year' since they were young? Pluto takes a long time to circle the Sun. Its highly eccentric orbit is due to Neptune's gravitational influence. The same physics that makes Pluto's orbit so long also means it overlaps with Neptune's for about 20 years. This delayed completion has real consequences for astronomers, as it means the New Horizons spacecraft will be the only one to visit Pluto until at least the 22nd century. Pluto won't complete its orbit until 2178, leaving us to wonder about the vastness of time.

Pluto's highly eccentric orbit is a reminder of the complexity of our solar system.
The next time you look up at the night sky, remember Pluto's eternal journey.
